jobs.description:
**Full-time | Remote | Onboarding**

### **About the Role**

Anchor Utility Company is looking for a Client Onboarding Specialist to help multifamily clients launch services such as Resident Billing, Utility Expense Management, and Vacant Cost Recovery. You’ll guide assigned properties from kickoff through setup in our billing platform, First Time Billing, client approval, and handoff to Operations.

You’ll be a primary point of contact for clients during onboarding. This role is a good fit if you enjoy working with clients, keeping several projects moving at once, and catching details that could affect a resident’s first bill.

### **What You’ll Do**

* Set expectations at kickoff, request required information, and keep clients informed about progress, next steps, and delays.
* Manage multiple property implementations at once. Track milestones and deadlines, follow up on open items, and escalate issues that could delay launch or first billing.
* Configure properties in our billing platform using client requirements, utility billing methods, supporting documentation, and applicable billing guidelines.
* Coordinate First Time Billing, review results for accuracy, work with internal teams to resolve discrepancies, and obtain client approval.
* Hand off each property to Operations with approved billing, complete documentation, and a clear record of any open items.
* Partner with Client Engagement, Operations, Accounting, Meter Solutions, and other teams to resolve issues, document processes, and improve how we onboard properties.

### **What You’ll Bring**

**Required**

* Prior experience in utility billing, property management, multifamily housing, or a related field.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain billing or setup steps clearly to clients and internal teams.
* Strong organization, time management, and attention to detail, with the ability to manage several projects and deadlines at once.
* Proactive follow-through and accountability for assigned work.
* Sound problem-solving skills and the ability to work independently, including knowing when to escalate an issue.
* Comfort learning new software, systems, and processes.

**Preferred**

* Direct experience with resident utility billing or utility expense management.
* Familiarity with ratio utility billing systems (RUBS), submetering, direct-billed utilities, or utility billing regulations.
* Experience with property management platforms such as Yardi, Entrata, or AppFolio.
* Experience in client onboarding, implementation, or account management.
* Experience reviewing utility invoices, billing reports, or financial documentation.

### **Why Join Us?**

* Competitive pay and a benefits package.
* A collaborative team that works across departments to help clients launch services successfully.
* Opportunities to develop your skills in client implementation, multifamily utility billing, and project coordination.

### **How to Apply**

Apply through Anchor Utility Company’s online employment application. We look forward to learning about your experience and how you’ve helped clients or properties through a successful transition.

**Anchor Utility is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.**

This role will lead the strategy and evolution of Field Medical onboarding and ongoing capability development, translating business needs, evolving scientific engagement expectations, adult learning principles, and emerging technologies into practical learning experiences that accelerate readiness, sustain effectiveness, and support continued growth in role.

The individual will work across therapeutic areas and functions to establish common learning standards while enabling appropriate customization for role, experience level, and therapeutic-area needs. The position has a future-focused orientation, regularly evaluating emerging trends in healthcare, scientific engagement, learning practices, technology, and AI to ensure Field Medical colleagues are prepared for an evolving external environment throughout their careers. Main responsibilities include:

  
  

* Partner closely with therapeutic-area Knowledge & Learning leads, Field Directors, and TA leadership to define onboarding objectives, learning pathways, and developmental milestones that support new hire preparedness and effectiveness in external scientific engagement.
* Design and maintain a connected learning and development approach that bridges onboarding with continuous education, professional skills development, and ongoing capability growth for tenured MSLs and field leaders.
* Partner with therapeutic-area leadership and subject matter experts to identify common enterprise learning needs and determine where customization is required.
* Apply adult learning, instructional design, and performance-support principles to create engaging, practical, and scalable learning experiences for colleagues at different career stages.
* Develop and continuously improve learning resources and experiences, including structured onboarding journeys, continuing education, workshops, simulations, practice opportunities, field-based learning, performance support, and self-directed resources.
* Identify and advance professional skills learning for MSLs, including capabilities such as communication, strategic thinking, business acumen, emotional intelligence, self-leadership, and AI fluency and judgment, aligned to evolving Field Medical expectations.
* Refine coaching resources and tools for Field Directors and other people leaders to strengthen their role in onboarding, field coaching, ongoing development, and application of learning.
* Support career development and continued capability growth by connecting onboarding and continuing education with broader professional capability and development frameworks.
* Incorporate emerging technologies, including AI-enabled learning and performance-support solutions, where they can improve learning effectiveness, personalization, accessibility, or efficiency.
* Create mechanisms to gather learner and stakeholder feedback, identify emerging capability gaps across both new and experienced colleagues, and translate insights into improvements in learning strategy and design.
  

  

**Preferred Qualifications:**

  
  

* Doctorate degree and 2 years of Medical Science Liaison, Medical Affairs, learning and development, or other relevant experience, OR
* Master's degree and 4 years of Medical Affairs, learning and development, instructional design, organizational development, or other relevant experience, OR
* Bachelor's degree and 6 years of Medical Affairs, learning and development, instructional design, organizational development, or other relevant experience

As we work to develop treatments that take care of others, we also work to care for your professional and personal growth and well-being. From our competitive benefits to our collaborative culture, we’ll support your journey every step of the way.

Effortless Office partners with our customers to make IT effortless so they can focus on their business. As a Hybrid Managed Services Provider (MSP) with a focus on providing world-class customer experience, we deliver and fully support secure cloud solutions as well as comprehensive managed IT and network services.
  
  
**About the Role:**  
The Talent Acquisition & Onboarding Coordinator partners with the Experience Manager to attract, hire, onboard, and develop the people who make Effortless Office special. This role supports the full hiring lifecycle, from interviewing candidates and completing background and reference checks to preparing and sending offer letters, and makes sure every new hire has a smooth, welcoming start. They coordinate onboarding and new hire training, track and process 45-day and 90-day performance reviews, and manage the annual company review cycle from kickoff through completion. With a strong eye for detail and a commitment to confidentiality, the Talent Acquisition & Onboarding Coordinator creates a consistent, effortless experience for every candidate and employee, from the first interview through every review.  
  
**Location:** 100% Remote  
**Reports To:** Experience Manager  
**Schedule:** Monday – Friday 8:00 am – 5:00 pm PST  
**Compensation:** $55,000 – $60,000 annually  
**Benefits:**

* Health, dental, and vision insurance
* 401K + employer match
* Paid time off and holidays
* Opportunities for career growth and development
* Formal and structured mentorship
* Training and certification support

  
**Responsibilities:**  
**Recruiting & Interviewing**

* Partner with the Experience Manager and hiring managers to understand staffing needs and post open positions on job boards and other recruiting channels.
* Screen resumes and applications and conduct initial screening interviews via Microsoft Teams to identify qualified candidates.
* Schedule and coordinate interviews, participate in interviews, and gather feedback from hiring teams.
* Communicate promptly and professionally with candidates throughout the hiring process and keep candidate records accurate and up to date.

**Background Checks, References & Offers**

* Initiate and track background checks, ensuring each is completed and cleared before a new hire’s start date.
* Conduct professional reference checks and summarize findings for the Experience Manager and hiring manager.
* Prepare and send offer letters, track acceptances, and confirm start dates with new hires and their managers.
* Handle all candidate and employee information with strict confidentiality and in line with company policy and employment regulations.

**Onboarding & New Hire Training**

* Coordinate onboarding from offer acceptance through the first 90 days, ensuring new hire paperwork and PEO enrollment are completed accurately and on time.
* Work with hiring managers, IT, and Accounting so new hires have the equipment, system access, and information they need on day one.
* Schedule and facilitate new hire orientation and training on company policies, core values, and our EOS (Entrepreneurial Operating System) practices.
* Track completion of required new hire training, including security awareness training.
* Serve as a go-to resource for new hires during their first weeks with the company.

**Performance Reviews**

* Schedule, track, and process 45-day and 90-day performance reviews for all new hires, ensuring they are completed on time.
* Prepare review materials for managers and follow up on outstanding or overdue reviews.
* Manage the annual company review cycle, including timelines, communications, manager reminders, and completion tracking.
* Maintain accurate review documentation and report on completion status and trends to the Experience Manager.

**Employee Experience & Continuous Improvement**

* Maintain organized, accurate, and confidential employee and hiring records.
* Develop and refine templates, checklists, and processes to create a consistent experience for candidates, new hires, and managers.
* Support the Experience Manager with employee engagement initiatives and other HR projects as needed.

* Bachelor’s degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, or related field preferred; equivalent experience will be considered.
* Preferred Certifications: aPHR, PHR, or SHRM-CP

* Accurately assesses brand impact and urgency to prioritize your queue
* Clear, complete written communication: brands, teammates, and Engineering can act on your updates without follow-up questions
* Strong written and verbal communication with brands and internal teams
* Precision in technical guidance: you confirm before you advise, especially on high-stakes launches
* Highly organized and reliable; you follow through on every account

----------------

* Experience in a startup or high-growth SaaS environment
* Familiarity with Intercom, Salesforce, or similar support and CRM tooling
* Knowledge of the creator economy, influencer marketing, or affiliate platforms
* Comfortable using AI tools (e.g., Fin AI, Claude, or similar) to work faster and spot gaps

About us and the role

Our mission is to help women build confidence in their health and fitness through practical guidance, sustainable habits and personal support. We value thoughtful communication, dependable follow-through and a positive client experience.

We’re looking for an experienced sales closer to welcome new customers and guide suitable customers toward personalised coaching.

Exclusive, company-generated warm leads are provided. You’ll speak with women who have already purchased from our health and fitness business, with onboarding appointments booked directly into your calendar.

You’ll help customers get started, understand their goals and assess whether additional coaching is suitable. You’ll own the conversation through qualification, enrollment and follow-up. You are not expected to source or purchase your own leads.

What you will do

* Lead friendly, focused onboarding calls and help customers get started.
* Understand each customer's goals, challenges and interest in additional support.
* Assess suitability for coaching and ask permission before moving into a sales conversation.
* Explain coaching inclusions, pricing and payment terms clearly and accurately.
* Handle questions and objections respectfully, complete suitable enrollments and agree clear next steps.
* Manage assigned customer opportunities, including appointment confirmations, rescheduling, missed-call follow-up and booking further conversations when needed.
* Keep CRM records accurate and give the coaching team a clear handover.
* Help every customer leave onboarding with a useful next step.
* Participate in call reviews, training and improvements to the customer experience.

Pay and working arrangements

This is a remote, full-time role based in the United States or Canada, with 40 paid hours per week, Monday to Friday, from 12pm to 8pm US Eastern Time, following US daylight saving time. Required onboarding, calls, follow-up, administration and training time are paid.

Pay is $25 USD per hour plus 10% commission on eligible collected coaching revenue, excluding tax and refunded amounts. The hourly base is not a recoverable draw. Commission depends on collected payments, with full attribution, payment timing and adjustment terms set out in the written compensation plan.

Potential total earnings after ramp-up are approximately $9,000 to $20,000 USD per month at 40 paid hours per week, including hourly pay and commission. This is a projection, not guaranteed income. Actual earnings depend on appointment volume, performance and eligible customer payments collected; ramp-up and installment timing can reduce monthly earnings.

Support and opportunities to grow

You’ll work closely with the team, with clear expectations, regular feedback and room to contribute your ideas. We’re looking to build lasting working relationships with people who care about helping women feel stronger and more confident.

We’re looking for someone who wants to grow with our company, take on greater responsibilities and earn opportunities for mentorship and sales leadership through strong performance as our team expands.

How to apply

Upload your CV or an exported professional profile and include a link to a 60 to 90-second Loom video or similar recording in the application form. Complete the screening questions with your location, availability, earliest start date and relevant experience. A phone number is required so we can arrange the next stage.  **Requirements**

* Proven consultative or high-ticket sales experience, including qualification and closing.
* Experience selling health, fitness or coaching services is preferred.
* A warm, clear phone manner, active listening and respectful objection handling.
* Experience helping customers get started with online services is a plus.
* Strong follow-up, CRM and calendar management habits.
* Availability for 40 paid hours per week, Monday to Friday, from 12pm to 8pm US Eastern Time, following US daylight saving time.

* Exclusive warm leads from existing paying customers, with onboarding appointments booked into your calendar.

**Location: Mid-Willamette Valley Area** ***(Salem area preferred)***

**Remote position with regular in-person trainings, presentations, and site visits across the region**

**Position Overview**

Skill Demand Energy is seeking a Technical Training Specialist to be the go-to educator for residential energy efficiency across our Energy Trust of Oregon programs. You’ll design and deliver training, presentations, and workshops that help community partners, contractors, and Skill Demand’s own teams understand home energy assessments, energy efficiency measures, and program requirements, and apply them correctly.

This role is for someone who enjoys teaching technical material and can engage an audience. You’ll take complex topics and make them clear and usable for audiences ranging from experienced contractors to retail associates and customer service staff. You’ll manage several training projects at once (building materials, scheduling sessions, coordinating with team leads, and keeping deadlines on track) while also serving as a technical resource for questions across our community programs.

The ideal candidate combines solid, hands-on knowledge of residential energy efficiency (BPI certification preferred) with proven experience developing and delivering training, strong organization, and the ability to work independently across multiple projects in a fast-paced environment.

**Why This Role Exists**

Skill Demand delivers energy efficiency programs through many channels: community organizations, contractors, retail outreach, and our Contact Center. All of them rely on accurate, consistent technical information.

As our programs grow, we need a dedicated technical educator to makes sure our staff and partners:

* Understands program requirements the same way
* Has practical, up-to-date resources they can actually use
* Catches technical and documentation issues before they become problems

**Key Responsibilities**

*Approximate time allocations are shown to give a sense of the role’s focus.*

***Technical Training, Education & Presentations (50%)***

* Design and deliver technical training, presentations, and workshops, in person and virtually, for community partners, contractors, and Skill Demand teams including Retail Outreach, Contact Center, and Community Outreach
* Develop training materials such as slide decks, job aids, quick-reference guides, checklists, and short how-to videos
* Translate complex topics (building science, assessment protocols, measure eligibility, documentation requirements) into clear, practical guidance suited to each audience
* Lead onboarding and refresher trainings for new partners and staff, and update content when program requirements or incentives change
* Maintain a training calendar and a central, current library of training materials
* Gather participant feedback and use it, along with recurring quality assurance and documentation errors, to improve training
* Coordinate with team leads so training supports each team’s goals

***Project & Workload Management***

* Manage multiple training projects and technical assignments at once, from planning through delivery
* Set timelines and milestones, track deliverables, and provide regular, brief status updates, including early notice when something is at risk
* Prioritize competing requests with your supervisor through an agreed intake process
* Keep organized records of training sessions, attendance, material versions, and follow-up items
* Use project management tools (such as Asana) to track work and keep progress visible to the team

***Technical Subject-Matter Support (20%)***

* Serve as Skill Demand’s technical resource on home energy assessments, measure eligibility, and program documentation and quality requirements
* Answer technical questions from internal teams and partners, and turn recurring questions into FAQs, job aids, or training updates
* Act as technical liaison between partners, processing teams, and program administrators
* Help reduce documentation and quality assurance errors by spotting patterns and addressing them through training

***Program Improvement & Special Projects (15%)***

* Recommend improvements to program workflows, documentation, and training resources based on patterns seen across teams
* Support the rollout of new tools and processes through training, user guides, and troubleshooting
* Provide technical support for Retail Outreach and other special projects as assigned, with agreed scope and deadlines
* Work with internal teams and program administrators to resolve technical issues

***Community Partner Technical Support (15%)***

* Provide scheduled technical training and assistance to assigned community partners
* Join partner meetings when technical expertise or training is needed, and document action items you own
* Build trusted working relationships with partner staff through clear, consistent follow-through
* Share recurring partner technical challenges with Community Outreach staff and recommend training-based solutions
* Flag technical issues that may affect partner milestones to Community Outreach leadership

**Required Qualifications**

* 3+ years of experience in residential energy efficiency, home performance, weatherization, or a related field
* 2+ years of experience developing and delivering technical training, presentations, or workshops for adult audiences
* Strong working knowledge of home energy assessments, energy efficiency measures, and program documentation and compliance
* Demonstrated ability to independently manage multiple projects with competing deadlines
* Proficiency with presentation and virtual meeting tools (PowerPoint or Google Slides, Zoom or Teams)
* Valid driver’s license and reliable transportation for regional travel

**Preferred Qualifications**

* BPI certification (e.g., Building Analyst) or comparable field credentials
* Spanish language proficiency, including the ability to deliver training in Spanish
* Experience working with community-based organizations, nonprofits, or income-qualified programs
* Experience with Energy Trust of Oregon or other utility or public-benefit energy programs
* Background in instructional design or adult learning (e.g., train-the-trainer experience, ATD or similar certification)
* Experience creating short training videos or e-learning content
* Experience with project management software such as Asana

**Core Competencies**

* Engaging presenter and skilled facilitator
* Turns technical detail into practical, audience-appropriate guidance
* Highly organized; manages multiple priorities and meets deadlines
* Takes initiative: identifies needs and moves work forward without waiting to be asked
* Strong technical credibility and sound judgment
* Collaborative and open to feedback
* Cultural humility and community-centered values

**Success in This Role Looks Like**

* Partners and Skill Demand staff have clear, current, easy-to-use technical training and resources
* Recurring technical and documentation errors decrease in areas covered by training
* Participants rate trainings as clear and useful
* Training projects are delivered on schedule, with progress visible to the team

**Who We Are**

**Skill Demand Energy** is a culturally diverse organization focused on expanding access to energy efficiency solutions that reduce household energy burden and strengthen communities. We work at the intersection of technical expertise, public-benefit programs, and community-based delivery—supporting both individuals and organizations in navigating energy incentives, program requirements, and long-term sustainability.

Our work is grounded in partnership, accountability, and continuous improvement. We believe effective energy programs are built through clear expectations, strong relationships, and respect for the lived experiences of the communities we serve. We are a growing, collaborative team that values initiative, adaptability, and thoughtful problem-solving, and we encourage candidates who are motivated by impact and learning to apply. We invest in sharing knowledge across our teams, and this role is at the center of that work.

Skill Demand Energy is deeply committed to Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion. We strive to build a workplace and programs that reflect the communities we serve, center equity in decision-making, and create inclusive systems where all people have access to opportunity, support, and success.

Pay: $80,000.00 - $85,000.00 per year

Benefits:

* 401(k)
* Health insurance
* Life insurance
* Paid time off
* Referral program

Application Question(s):

* Do you have at least 3 years of experience in residential energy efficiency, home performance, weatherization, or a related field?
* Do you have at least 2 years of experience developing and delivering technical training, presentations, or workshops for adult audiences?
* Do you have a valid driver's license and reliable transportation for regional travel?

jobs.title: Senior Implementation Consultant, Logis Dispatch
jobs.description:
**Senior Implementation Consultant, Logis Dispatch**

**Team:** Implementation, Logis · **Level:** Senior Implementation Consultant · **Reports to:** Team Lead, Implementation (Logis Dispatch) · **Location:** Remote, United States

**Outcome.** Dispatch centers go live on Logis Dispatch on the planned date, right the first time, and trust the system from the first call.

**About the role**

A dispatch center cannot stop to go live. When we implement Logis Dispatch, we change the system a center uses to send help to every call, on a floor that runs 24 hours a day. A good go-live is quiet. A bad one is felt on the next emergency.

You lead our most complex Logis Dispatch implementations from kickoff to handoff: discovery of how the center works today, configuration, interfaces, data, training, and the cutover itself. You are the senior voice on the team, the one others come to when a project gets hard.

**Where we are headed**

Logis Dispatch is growing across North America and Europe, and into new kinds of customers such as mobile integrated health programs. The product is moving to the cloud and the browser, which will change how fast a center can go live.

You will lead the projects that set the standard, and help design the faster way we will implement next.

**Who ESO is**

ESO is the first responder for the first responders. We build software and data products for EMS agencies, fire departments, hospitals, and government stakeholders, and serve more than 18,000 customers. Our mission is to improve community health and safety outcomes through the power of data.

**How you support the mission**

You support the mission by making sure dispatchers can trust the system in front of them from the first call after cutover. When a center goes live well, crews get to calls faster and leaders can see what is working.

You support your team by setting the standard: you follow the playbook, improve it, and help newer consultants run their first go-lives.

**What you will do**

**Lead each implementation**

* Own a set of Logis Dispatch implementations, including the largest and most complex, each on a dated plan in the project management platform with health, risks, and next steps current every week.

* Run discovery with the center: call types, response plans, units and stations, geography, and the workflows of call-takers, dispatchers, and supervisors.

* Raise risks early to your team lead and the customer, with a plan to recover.

**Configure, connect, and cut over**

* Configure Logis Dispatch to the configuration standards, including mapping and unit recommendations.

* Work with Integration Engineering on interfaces: ePCR, billing, mapping and vehicle location, telephony, and paging.

* Plan and run the cutover with the center, often on site, with a rollback plan and a go or no-go call.

**Train, hand off, and raise the bar**

* Train call-takers, dispatchers, supervisors, and administrators on the workflows they will use every shift.

* Hand off cleanly at go-live: Logis Dispatch support in Customer Care owns tickets, and Customer Success owns the relationship.

* Mentor newer consultants and keep the implementation playbook current with what each project teaches us.

**Time tracking**

* Log your time in real time, as you finish each issue or task, in the time tracking system, by customer and type of work.

**How success is measured**

* Go-lives on the date in the project plan, and right the first time, with no serious incident caused by the setup in the first 30 days.

* Time to value: days from kickoff to the center running live calls in Logis Dispatch, against the standard for the project size.

* Every project plan current each week: dates, health, and next steps.

* Customer satisfaction (CSAT) at go-live and at handoff.

* Clean handoffs: tickets in the first 60 days after go-live go to support, not back to you.

* Time logged in real time and completely, to the team standard.

**Your first** **90 days**

**By day 30.** Systems access; Logis Dispatch configuration standards and the playbook learned; met every customer in your set and taken over each project plan.

**By day 60.** Every project in your set on a current, dated plan. First discovery or configuration milestone delivered to the checklist.

**By day 90.** Owning your full set of implementations, with a cutover planned or delivered, and mentoring at least one newer consultant.

**Dispatch and emergency communications fundamentals**

You bring these on day one, at the depth of someone who has implemented or run a dispatch system:

* How a call moves through a communication center: call-taking, triage, dispatch, unit status, and closing the incident.

* The parts of a dispatch system and what each user does in it: call-takers, dispatchers, supervisors, and field crews on mobile.

* What connects to the dispatch system and why it matters: ePCR, records management, mapping and vehicle location, radio, telephony, and paging.

* What a bad day looks like on a dispatch floor, and why a slow answer from us is a problem for the people they serve.

**How you grow here**

We grow people through skill badges: short, practical certifications in our products and in the craft of the role. Your badges shape your development plan and open the next role.

* **By day 90:** The Logis Dispatch implementation badges: discovery, configuration standards, interfaces, cutover, and training. Plus the AI working badge: one cutover plan drafted with the assistant and reviewed to standard.

* **By 12 months:** The advanced badges: multi-agency and international projects, recovering a project that has slipped, and certifying new consultants. Plus the validator badge: signing off assistant-drafted project status for your set.

* **Where it leads:** Team Lead, Implementation (Logis Dispatch); Integration Engineering, Logis; or a Success Specialist or CSM role for dispatch customers.

**Tools you will use**

**Tool**

**What you use it for**

Project management platform

Every project plan, its dates, health, and next steps

Customer relationship management (CRM) system

The handoff from Sales: scope and what was promised

Logis Dispatch

Configuration, and the test system for rehearsing the cutover

Ticketing system

Escalations during and just after go-live

Customer success platform

Account health, shared with Customer Success

Team chat

Quick questions and coordination with your team and other teams

Time tracking system

Your time by customer and type of work

AI workspace and assistants

First drafts of configuration checks, cutover plans, training material, and customer updates inside the project platform; you review every one.

**What you bring**

**Who does well here**

You will do well here if you have implemented a dispatch system or run one in a communications center, have led live cutovers, and want bigger and more complex projects.

You will also do well if you are a strong implementer ready for the senior seat, and hungry to be the person others come to.

**Required**

* Four or more years implementing dispatch or other public-safety software, or running the system in a 911 or dispatch center.

* You have planned and led a live cutover on a working dispatch floor.

* Comfort with how systems connect: interfaces, mapping, and data moving between systems.

* You run several complex projects at once, and you stay calm and clear with a customer under pressure.

* Able to travel for on-site go-lives.

**Nice to have**

* Experience with Logis Dispatch.

* A dispatcher or telecommunicator background, or EMD or EFD certification.

* Experience with multi-agency, mobile integrated health (MIH), or international dispatch projects.

If you meet most of this and the work excites you, apply. We would rather talk with a strong candidate who took a different path than miss one.

**How the role fits**

**Team and level**

**Implementation, Logis · Senior Implementation Consultant**

Reports to

Team Lead, Implementation (Logis Dispatch), under the Director of Implementation, Logis

Leads

No one; mentors newer consultants

Works closely with

Integration Engineering, Logis; Logis Dispatch support in Customer Care; Customer Success, Logis

**How you will use AI**

**Today:** AI helps draft configuration checks, cutover plans, training material, and customer updates; you review every one.

**Where we are heading:** More of the checking and documenting done by AI, so you spend your time with the center and on the hard configuration questions.

**What stays with you:** The go or no-go call on a cutover, any change to a live dispatch system, and every conversation with a customer about a problem. If an AI assistant drafted it and you signed it, it is yours. You can stop any automated step on your work, and we expect you to when something looks wrong.

**Agents you work with**

Some of your colleagues are software. These are the assistants that draft, check, and flag work for this role today or in the coming year:

* **The project assistant:** Drafts your weekly plan health and flags slipped dates; you confirm before it is published.

* **The Logis knowledge assistant:** Answers configuration and product questions from the product itself; you check the answer before it reaches the center.

* **The capacity engine:** Reads your plans nightly and raises late go-lives and load to the council; the go or no-go call stays yours.

You confirm or correct what they produce before it reaches a customer or a record. Their work counts only when the measures above hold.

**Why ESO**

We build technology for people who run toward emergencies. That sense of purpose runs through how we hire, how we build, and how we show up for our customers. You will work alongside people who care about the communities first responders serve, in a remote, collaborative team that invests in your growth.

**Benefits & Perks**

ESO offers a comprehensive suite of benefits to promote health and financial security for our employees and their families. For full-time employment you this includes:

* Competitive health plans (medical, dental, & vision insurance)
* PTO (starting at 20 days) & 12 company holidays
* 401(k) with company match
* Telemedicine service provided by ESO
* Savings accounts (FSA, HSA, DCA)
* Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
* Annual health and wellness reimbursement
* Peace of mind benefits such as life insurance, disability insurance, and worksite benefits
* Paid parental leave, new child program, & flexible parental return-to-work options
* Casual office environments and unlimited office snacks and drinks

**About ESO**

ESO is a fast-paced, growing data, technology, and research company passionate about improving community health and safety through the power of data. We pioneer innovative, user-friendly software to meet the changing needs of today's EMS agencies, fire departments, and hospitals. We're small enough to be nimble and fun, but big enough to be a great place to work. We serve thousands of customers out of our offices across the US, Canada and Northern Ireland.

Are you ready to Make a Difference? At ESO, we believe in bringing your true self to work every single day. If you don't match all the qualifications on the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway! We are looking for passionate, innovative, and authentic people to help drive our mission.

All offers are contingent upon a successful background check.

  

*ESO is committed to creating a diverse and inclusive work environment and is proud to be an equal opportunity and affirmative action employer. We invite you to consider opportunities at ESO regardless of your gender; gender identity; gender reassignment; age; religion; race; national origin; political affiliation; sexual orientation; disability; veteran status; or other non-merit factor.*

jobs.title: Senior Implementation Consultant, Logis Dispatch
jobs.description:
**Team:** Implementation, Logis · **Level:** Senior Implementation Consultant · **Reports to:** Team Lead, Implementation (Logis Dispatch) · **Location:** Remote, United States

**Outcome.** Dispatch centers go live on Logis Dispatch on the planned date, right the first time, and trust the system from the first call.

**About the role**

A dispatch center cannot stop to go live. When we implement Logis Dispatch, we change the system a center uses to send help to every call, on a floor that runs 24 hours a day. A good go-live is quiet. A bad one is felt on the next emergency.

You lead our most complex Logis Dispatch implementations from kickoff to handoff: discovery of how the center works today, configuration, interfaces, data, training, and the cutover itself. You are the senior voice on the team, the one others come to when a project gets hard.

**Where we are headed**

Logis Dispatch is growing across North America and Europe, and into new kinds of customers such as mobile integrated health programs. The product is moving to the cloud and the browser, which will change how fast a center can go live.

You will lead the projects that set the standard, and help design the faster way we will implement next.

**Who ESO is**

ESO is the first responder for the first responders. We build software and data products for EMS agencies, fire departments, hospitals, and government stakeholders, and serve more than 18,000 customers. Our mission is to improve community health and safety outcomes through the power of data.

**How you support the mission**

You support the mission by making sure dispatchers can trust the system in front of them from the first call after cutover. When a center goes live well, crews get to calls faster and leaders can see what is working.

You support your team by setting the standard: you follow the playbook, improve it, and help newer consultants run their first go-lives.

**What you will do**

**Lead each implementation**

* Own a set of Logis Dispatch implementations, including the largest and most complex, each on a dated plan in the project management platform with health, risks, and next steps current every week.

* Run discovery with the center: call types, response plans, units and stations, geography, and the workflows of call-takers, dispatchers, and supervisors.

* Raise risks early to your team lead and the customer, with a plan to recover.

**Configure, connect, and cut over**

* Configure Logis Dispatch to the configuration standards, including mapping and unit recommendations.

* Work with Integration Engineering on interfaces: ePCR, billing, mapping and vehicle location, telephony, and paging.

* Plan and run the cutover with the center, often on site, with a rollback plan and a go or no-go call.

**Train, hand off, and raise the bar**

* Train call-takers, dispatchers, supervisors, and administrators on the workflows they will use every shift.

* Hand off cleanly at go-live: Logis Dispatch support in Customer Care owns tickets, and Customer Success owns the relationship.

* Mentor newer consultants and keep the implementation playbook current with what each project teaches us.

**Time tracking**

* Log your time in real time, as you finish each issue or task, in the time tracking system, by customer and type of work.

**How success is measured**

* Go-lives on the date in the project plan, and right the first time, with no serious incident caused by the setup in the first 30 days.

* Time to value: days from kickoff to the center running live calls in Logis Dispatch, against the standard for the project size.

* Every project plan current each week: dates, health, and next steps.

* Customer satisfaction (CSAT) at go-live and at handoff.

* Clean handoffs: tickets in the first 60 days after go-live go to support, not back to you.

* Time logged in real time and completely, to the team standard.

**Your first** **90 days**

**By day 30.** Systems access; Logis Dispatch configuration standards and the playbook learned; met every customer in your set and taken over each project plan.

**By day 60.** Every project in your set on a current, dated plan. First discovery or configuration milestone delivered to the checklist.

**By day 90.** Owning your full set of implementations, with a cutover planned or delivered, and mentoring at least one newer consultant.

**Dispatch and emergency communications fundamentals**

You bring these on day one, at the depth of someone who has implemented or run a dispatch system:

* How a call moves through a communication center: call-taking, triage, dispatch, unit status, and closing the incident.

* The parts of a dispatch system and what each user does in it: call-takers, dispatchers, supervisors, and field crews on mobile.

* What connects to the dispatch system and why it matters: ePCR, records management, mapping and vehicle location, radio, telephony, and paging.

* What a bad day looks like on a dispatch floor, and why a slow answer from us is a problem for the people they serve.

**How you grow here**

We grow people through skill badges: short, practical certifications in our products and in the craft of the role. Your badges shape your development plan and open the next role.

* **By day 90:** The Logis Dispatch implementation badges: discovery, configuration standards, interfaces, cutover, and training. Plus the AI working badge: one cutover plan drafted with the assistant and reviewed to standard.

* **By 12 months:** The advanced badges: multi-agency and international projects, recovering a project that has slipped, and certifying new consultants. Plus the validator badge: signing off assistant-drafted project status for your set.

* **Where it leads:** Team Lead, Implementation (Logis Dispatch); Integration Engineering, Logis; or a Success Specialist or CSM role for dispatch customers.

**Tools you will use**

**Tool**

**What you use it for**

  

Project management platform

Every project plan, its dates, health, and next steps

  

Customer relationship management (CRM) system

The handoff from Sales: scope and what was promised

  

Logis Dispatch

Configuration, and the test system for rehearsing the cutover

  

Ticketing system

Escalations during and just after go-live

  

Customer success platform

Account health, shared with Customer Success

  

Team chat

Quick questions and coordination with your team and other teams

  

Time tracking system

Your time by customer and type of work

  

AI workspace and assistants

First drafts of configuration checks, cutover plans, training material, and customer updates inside the project platform; you review every one.

**What you bring**

**Who does well here**

You will do well here if you have implemented a dispatch system or run one in a communications center, have led live cutovers, and want bigger and more complex projects.

You will also do well if you are a strong implementer ready for the senior seat, and hungry to be the person others come to.

**Required**

* Four or more years implementing dispatch or other public-safety software, or running the system in a 911 or dispatch center.

* You have planned and led a live cutover on a working dispatch floor.

* Comfort with how systems connect: interfaces, mapping, and data moving between systems.

* You run several complex projects at once, and you stay calm and clear with a customer under pressure.

* Able to travel for on-site go-lives.

**Nice to have**

* Experience with Logis Dispatch.

* A dispatcher or telecommunicator background, or EMD or EFD certification.

* Experience with multi-agency, mobile integrated health (MIH), or international dispatch projects.

If you meet most of this and the work excites you, apply. We would rather talk with a strong candidate who took a different path than miss one.

**How the role fits**

**Team and level**

**Implementation, Logis · Senior Implementation Consultant**

  

Reports to

Team Lead, Implementation (Logis Dispatch), under the Director of Implementation, Logis

  

Leads

No one; mentors newer consultants

  

Works closely with

Integration Engineering, Logis; Logis Dispatch support in Customer Care; Customer Success, Logis

**How you will use AI**

**Today:** AI helps draft configuration checks, cutover plans, training material, and customer updates; you review every one.

**Where we are heading:** More of the checking and documenting done by AI, so you spend your time with the center and on the hard configuration questions.

**What stays with you:** The go or no-go call on a cutover, any change to a live dispatch system, and every conversation with a customer about a problem. If an AI assistant drafted it and you signed it, it is yours. You can stop any automated step on your work, and we expect you to when something looks wrong.

**Agents you work with**

Some of your colleagues are software. These are the assistants that draft, check, and flag work for this role today or in the coming year:

* **The project assistant:** Drafts your weekly plan health and flags slipped dates; you confirm before it is published.

* **The Logis knowledge assistant:** Answers configuration and product questions from the product itself; you check the answer before it reaches the center.

* **The capacity engine:** Reads your plans nightly and raises late go-lives and load to the council; the go or no-go call stays yours.

You confirm or correct what they produce before it reaches a customer or a record. Their work counts only when the measures above hold.

**Why ESO**

We build technology for people who run toward emergencies. That sense of purpose runs through how we hire, how we build, and how we show up for our customers. You will work alongside people who care about the communities first responders serve, in a remote, collaborative team that invests in your growth.

**Benefits & Perks**

ESO offers a comprehensive suite of benefits to promote health and financial security for our employees and their families. For full-time employment you this includes:

* Competitive health plans (medical, dental, & vision insurance)
* PTO (starting at 20 days) & 12 company holidays
* 401(k) with company match
* Telemedicine service provided by ESO
* Savings accounts (FSA, HSA, DCA)
* Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
* Annual health and wellness reimbursement
* Peace of mind benefits such as life insurance, disability insurance, and worksite benefits
* Paid parental leave, new child program, & flexible parental return-to-work options
* Casual office environments and unlimited office snacks and drinks

**About ESO**

ESO is a fast-paced, growing data, technology, and research company passionate about improving community health and safety through the power of data. We pioneer innovative, user-friendly software to meet the changing needs of today’s EMS agencies, fire departments, and hospitals. We’re small enough to be nimble and fun, but big enough to be a great place to work. We serve thousands of customers out of our offices across the US, Canada and Northern Ireland.

Are you ready to Make a Difference? At ESO, we believe in bringing your true self to work every single day. If you don’t match all the qualifications on the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway! We are looking for passionate, innovative, and authentic people to help drive our mission.

All offers are contingent upon a successful background check.

*ESO is committed to creating a diverse and inclusive work environment and is proud to be an equal opportunity and affirmative action employer. We invite you to consider opportunities at ESO regardless of your gender; gender identity; gender reassignment; age; religion; race; national origin; political affiliation; sexual orientation; disability; veteran status; or other non-merit factor.*
